paragraphs: ## The Lion and the Mouse
A big lion was sleeping under a tree. A little mouse ran across his face. The lion woke up and was very angry. He caught the mouse with his big paw.
“Please let me go,” said the mouse. “I am very small, but one day I can help you. I promise.”
The lion laughed. “You? Help me? That is very funny!” But he opened his paw, and the mouse ran away.
A few days later, some hunters caught the lion in a net. They tied him to a tree with strong ropes. The lion roared and roared, but he could not get free.
The mouse heard the noise and ran to the lion. “Don’t be afraid,” he said. He began to bite the ropes with his sharp little teeth. Soon the ropes broke, and the lion was free.
“Now you know,” said the mouse with a smile. “A small friend can be a big help.”
Be kind to everyone, because even a small friend can help you.
## The Ants and the Grasshopper
It was a hot summer day. The ants were working hard. They carried seeds and grain to their home under the ground. The grain was heavy, but the ants did not stop.
A grasshopper sat on a leaf and watched them. He had a little violin, and he played a happy song.
“Why do you work so hard?” he asked. “Come and sing with me!”
“We must get ready for winter,” said one ant. “Winter is long, and we can run out of food. You should make a plan too.”
The grasshopper laughed. “Winter is far away. Now is the time to have fun!”
So the ants worked all summer, and the grasshopper sang all summer.
Then winter came. Snow covered the fields, and there was no food anywhere. At last the hungry grasshopper knocked on the ants’ door.
“Please give me some food,” he said sadly. “I have nothing to eat.”
The ant looked at him. “In summer we worked, and you sang,” she said. “Now we have only enough food for ourselves.”
The grasshopper went away, hungry and cold.
Work today, so you are ready for the hard days.
## The Hare and the Tortoise
A hare was very proud of his legs. “I am the fastest animal in the forest,” he said every day. “Nobody can run like me!”
One morning he saw a tortoise on the road. She was walking very slowly, and the hare laughed at her. “You are so slow! Do you ever get anywhere?”
“I get there in the end,” said the tortoise quietly. “Let’s have a race, you and I.”
The hare laughed and laughed. “A race? With you? All right!”
The fox was the judge. He drew a line on the ground and shouted, “Ready, steady, go!”
The hare ran like the wind. In a minute he could not see the tortoise at all. The tortoise walked on, one slow step after another, and she never stopped.
Halfway to the end, the hare stopped. “This is too easy,” he said. “I will have a little sleep under this tree.” Soon he was fast asleep.
The tortoise walked past the sleeping hare and kept going. She was tired, but she did not stop.
At last the hare woke up. He ran as fast as he could, but it was too late. The tortoise was already at the end of the road, and all the animals were shouting her name.
Slow and steady wins the race.
## The Shepherd’s Boy and the Wolf
Once there was a boy. His job was to look after the village sheep. Every day he sat on a hill and watched them. It was boring, and he had nobody to talk to.
One day he thought of a way to have some fun. “Wolf! Wolf!” he shouted. “A wolf is eating the sheep! Help me!”
The men dropped their work and ran up the hill. But there was no wolf. The boy laughed and laughed. “Ha ha! It was a joke!”
A few days later, he wanted to play a trick on them again. “Wolf! Wolf!” he shouted. Again the men ran up the hill, and again there was no wolf.
Then one evening a real wolf came out of the forest. The boy’s legs began to shake. “Wolf! Wolf!” he cried. “A real wolf! Please help me!”
In the village, the men heard him. “He is telling the same lie again,” they said. “We will not go this time.” Nobody came.
That night the wolf had a very big dinner. The boy went home with tears in his eyes and no sheep.
Nobody believes a liar, even when he tells the truth.
## The Crow and the Pitcher
It was a very hot summer. There was no rain for weeks, and the rivers were dry. A thirsty crow flew over the fields and looked for water.
At last he saw a pitcher near a farm. “Water!” he thought, and he flew down to it.
But the pitcher was tall and thin, and the water was very low. His beak was not long enough. He tried to push the pitcher over, but it was too heavy.
“What can I do?” he said. “I don’t want to give up.” He sat and thought for a long time.
Then he saw some small stones on the ground. “I have an idea!” he said. He picked up a stone and dropped it into the pitcher. Plop! One by one, the stones went in, and slowly the water came up.
At last the water was high enough. The crow drank and drank, and he was very proud of his clever idea.
When you really need something, you find a way.
## The Fox and the Grapes
One hot afternoon, a hungry fox walked through a farmer’s field. She had no breakfast and no lunch, and her stomach made a loud noise.
Then she looked up. High on a vine hung some big, purple grapes. They looked sweet and juicy.
“Lunch!” said the fox. She jumped, but the grapes were too high. She ran very fast and jumped as high as she could. Still nothing. She tried again and again, until her legs hurt.
At last she sat down, tired and angry. A little bird in a tree was watching her.
The fox looked up at the grapes and lifted her nose. “I don’t want them anyway,” she said. “They are sour. Only a fool wants sour grapes.”
Then she walked away with her head high, and the little bird laughed.
It is easy to say you do not want something you cannot have.
## The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
A country mouse lived in a small hole in a field. His life was quiet and simple. He ate seeds, roots and a little corn. It was not a lot of food, but he was happy.
One day his cousin, a town mouse, came to visit. She looked at his dinner and made a face. “Poor cousin! Come to the town with me. In my house there is a lot of food, and it is delicious.”
The country mouse was excited. They walked all night and came to a big house in the town.
The dining room was beautiful. On the table there was bread, cheese, cakes and sweet fruit. The country mouse’s eyes were very big. He took a bite of the cheese. It was the best food of his life.
Suddenly the door opened. “Run!” shouted the town mouse. They ran into a small hole in the wall, and their hearts beat fast. The cook walked in, took a plate and walked out again.
“It is nothing,” said the town mouse. “Let’s go on with our dinner.” But then a big cat jumped on the table! The two mice ran away again, even faster than before.
At last the country mouse spoke in a small voice. “Thank you, cousin, but I am going home. Your food is wonderful, but you are afraid all the time. At home I eat simple food, but I eat in peace.”
Simple food in peace is better than a rich dinner in fear.
## The North Wind and the Sun
One day the North Wind and the Sun had an argument. “I am stronger than you,” said the Wind. “No, I am stronger,” said the Sun.
Just then, a man came down the road. He was wearing a thick, warm coat.
“Let’s have a test,” said the Sun. “Which of us can make that man take off his coat? That one is stronger.”

“Easy!” said the North Wind. “Watch me.” He took a deep breath and blew hard. The trees shook, and dust flew everywhere. But the man held his coat tight. The Wind blew harder and harder, and the man held his coat tighter and tighter. At last the Wind ran out of breath and stopped.

“Now it is my turn,” said the Sun gently. She came out from behind a cloud and began to shine. The air became warm. Soon the man felt very hot. He wiped his face, and then he took off his coat and sat down by a river.
“I did it,” said the Sun. “And I did not need to shout.”
Being kind works better than being strong.

glossary.pitcher: testi, uzun ve dar ağızlı su kabı
glossary.sour: ekşi (hikâyede: elde edemediği şeyi küçümsemek için söylenen söz)
glossary.country: kır, kırsal bölge (Country Mouse = Kır Faresi)

quiz.q: How does the mouse help the lion?
options: He brings the lion some food
He bites the ropes
He shows the hunters the wrong way
He calls the other animals
quiz.explainTr: Fare, aslanı bağlayan ipleri keskin dişleriyle kemirir ve aslan özgür kalır.

quiz.q: Why does the grasshopper have nothing to eat in winter?
options: The ants take his food
He loses his violin
He does not like the food
He sang all summer and did not get food ready
quiz.explainTr: Çekirge yaz boyunca şarkı söyler, kış için yiyecek hazırlamaz. Karıncalar ise çalışmıştır.

quiz.q: Why does nobody come when the real wolf comes?
options: The men think the boy is lying again
The men are afraid of the wolf
The men cannot hear the boy
The men are asleep
quiz.explainTr: Çoban çocuk daha önce yalan söylediği için köylüler bu sefer de şaka yaptığını sanır.

quiz.q: Why does the country mouse go home?
options: He does not like cheese
He is too tired to eat
He is afraid in the town and wants peace
He wants a bigger house
quiz.explainTr: Şehirde sürekli korku içinde yaşamak istemez; evinde sade yemek yer ama huzurludur.

quiz.q: How does the Sun win the test?
options: He blows very hard
He shines and makes the man warm
He hides behind a cloud all day
He asks the man for his coat
quiz.explainTr: Güneş nazikçe ısıtır; adam sıcaktan paltosunu çıkarır. Rüzgâr ise ne kadar eserse adam o kadar sıkı sarılmıştır.
